item.title: Chebyshev-expanded covariant density functional from relativistic Brueckner theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.36299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a density-dependent covariant energy density functional (CE-ME1) from full-Dirac-space relativistic Brueckner--Hartree--Fock (RBHF) self-energies and the corresponding equation of state. The space-like component $U_V$ is incorporated at the Fermi surface through reduced scalar and time-like self-energies, which are mapped onto local Hartree $\sigma$, $\omega$, $\delta$, and $\rho$ channels. The density-dependent couplings are represented by cubic Chebyshev polynomials over the density range $0.08\leq\rho\leq0.48~{\rm fm}^{-3}$. A constrained thermodynamic calibration uses 199 RBHF energy-per-particle values from published microscopic computations at six isospin asymmetries, while maintaining positive, monotonic couplings. The Bonn-A RBHF saturation point, incompressibility $K_\infty=258$ MeV, symmetry energy $J=33.1$ MeV, and slope $L=65.2$ MeV are reproduced. The predicted curvature $K_{\rm sym}=33$ MeV differs from the published RBHF value of $-67$ MeV, illustrating the derivative sensitivity of the local reduction. The combined energy RMS is $0.613$ MeV, measuring model discrepancy rather than statistical uncertainty. Uniform matter remains mechanically stable and causal above saturation within the calibrated range. In cold charge-neutral $npe\mu$ matter, CE-ME1 reasonably reproduces the interpolated RBHF pressure and proton fraction over most of the interval, although the pressure discrepancy increases near its upper edge. The DD-ME2 benchmark is stiffer and predicts a lower proton fraction at high density.
item.dc:creator: Armen Sedrakian

item.title: Side jump and anomalous Lorentz transformation of a coherent Dirac wave packet
item.description: arXiv:2610.36416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin-orbit coupling makes the mean position of a spinning particle transform anomalously under a Lorentz boost, with an additional shift known as a side jump. In this work, we develop a trace method to derive an exact but compact transformation kernel for the probability center of a general three-dimensional Dirac wave packet under an arbitrary finite Lorentz boost. The expression includes the physics of finite momentum width, spin-momentum correlations, and coherent phase structure without a semi-classical expansion. We identify texture-dependent side jumps even at fixed initial mean momentum, spin, and orbital angular momentum, as well as a non-monotonic mass dependence for Gaussian packets at fixed momentum width. The explicit kernels further resolve the spin and orbital angular-momentum contributions for massive and massless fermions, providing a kinematic basis for covariant particle-based spin transport that retains wave-packet information.
item.dc:creator: Jin-Rui Wu, Shuai Y. F. Liu

item.title: Extracting the QCD speed of sound in the presence of quantum fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2610.36846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The equation of state of strongly interacting matter plays a %is one of the central quantities characterizing central role in characterizing quark--gluon plasma created in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. It has recently been recognized that the QCD speed of sound is responsible for the linear correlations between the mean transverse momentum and charged-particle multiplicity in ultra-central collisions. In realistic collisions, however, this thermodynamic correlation is inevitably biased by quantum-initiated event-by-event fluctuations. In this work, we present a novel statistical framework to correct this bias by leveraging the Gaussianity condition of the quantum fluctuations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this approach can also serve as a probe of thermalization. Validated by the event-by-event hydrodynamic simulations, the extracted speed of sound in our framework is successfully consistent with the predictions from lattice QCD, from large to small collision systems.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Shan Mu, Li Yan, Xu-Guang Huang

item.title: Density-Dependent Description of Clustering in Axially-Symmetric Nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.36872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a microscopic description of the {\alpha}-decay processes from axially-symmetric superfluid nuclei in terms of proton ({\pi}) and neutron ({\nu}) single-particle (sp) degrees of freedom within a standard Woods-Saxon mean field (WSMF) and a density-dependent clustering potential centered around the average Mott point of the nuclear density, where the {\alpha}-particle is formed. In this way the clustering process is automatically enhanced on the nuclear surface. As an illustration of the method, a systematics of {\alpha}-decay from even-even emitters is presented.
item.dc:creator: A. Dumitrescu, D. S. Delion

item.title: Phenomenology of strangeness-changing two-body currents in antineutrino scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.36906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Antineutrinos produce hyperons without kaons through Cabibbo-suppressed quasi-elastic scattering on a single nucleon. A two-body current acting on a correlated nucleon pair, nubar [NN] -> l+ Y N', gives the same hyperons plus a second nucleon. A companion paper constructs this current without fixing its size. StrangeMC, the only generator with the channel, set it to a flat 15% of the quasi-elastic hyperon cross section. We determine the ratio f = sigma_2p2h/sigma_QE of the two-body to the quasi-elastic hyperon cross section on carbon versus antineutrino energy, and the detector signatures of two-body events. The strange two-body current and its non-strange counterpart are computed on the same nucleon pair. Their ratio is converted into f with the Valencia non-strange 2p2h and quasi-elastic cross sections for carbon, assuming that nuclear effects missing from the pair are common to both. Under this assumption f rises from 0.14 at 0.6 GeV to 0.20-0.22 at 2-5 GeV. Averaged over the Booster antineutrino spectra it is 0.15-0.17, close to the 15% placeholder, which StrangeMC now replaces with f(E). The largest evaluated uncertainty comes from separating the two-body current from one-body production followed by rescattering: across the separation prescriptions explored, f at 1 GeV ranges from 0.12 to 0.22. Interference with one-body production is not calculated and could be as large as the two-body rate. In a simulated SBND antineutrino-mode exposure on argon with the carbon f, two-body events are about 11% of events that produce a strange hadron. They supply more than a quarter of the kaon-less Sigma+ events used to tag hyperon charge exchange, partly as Sigma+ made at the weak vertex. They reconstruct 12-30% low in energy under the quasi-elastic hypothesis. After final-state interactions half of them have a proton above 40 MeV at the vertex, against a fifth of quasi-elastic events.
item.dc:creator: Jarosalw A. Nowak

item.title: Systematic calculations of \beta-delayed fission probabilities using a microscopic framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.37088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The process of $\beta$-delayed fission ($\beta$DF) consists of a mother nucleus $\beta$-decaying to different states of a daughter isotope, followed by fission of the latter with a probability that strongly depends on the energy of the states populated in the $\beta$ decay. Studying this process experimentally can be challenging due to the typically small $\beta$DF probabilities. The theoretical framework presented in this work was developed to globally characterise $\beta$DF probabilities. This approach uses energy density functional based models to obtain the necessary inputs for the final probabilities, which are obtained through the nuclear reaction code TALYS. Calculations were performed for all isotopes with an experimentally measured value of $\beta$DF probabilities. Following the optimisation of the theoretical framework to better reproduce known data, a global RMS deviation of about two orders of magnitude was achieved, an accuracy that can be used to identify promising cases for future experimental $\beta$DF studies.
item.dc:creator: S. Bara, T. E. Cocolios, S. Goriely, W. Ryssens, A. S\'anchez-Fern\'andez, P. Van Duppen

item.title: On-shell reduction of spin-zero Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau covariants and implications for the relativistic impulse approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.37263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the on-shell content of the local Lorentz covariants of the five-dimensional spin-zero Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau algebra in elastic spin-zero-spin-$1/2$ scattering. The scalar, vector, and tensor structures are reduced explicitly to the two independent amplitudes allowed by the physical parity-conserving process. The two scalar structures are proportional on shell, the genuine nonminimal vector $i[P,\beta^\mu]$ is longitudinal and vanishes after contraction with the conserved fermion vector current, and the projected vectors $P\beta^\mu$ and $\beta^\mu P$ each reduce to one half of the minimal-vector contribution. The tensor covariants introduce no additional on-shell directions. We discuss the consequences for the four invariant choices used in meson-nucleus optical-potential calculations and show that different nuclear equations can arise only after on-shell-equivalent representatives are promoted to optical operators and iterated beyond the order at which the elementary impulse approximation is fixed. These results provide a systematic basis for distinguishing genuinely independent elementary amplitudes from representation-dependent effects generated by the optical embedding.
item.dc:creator: Luis B. Castro

item.title: Covariant Wigner function and spin polarization of the Rarita-Schwinger field
item.description: arXiv:2610.37382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the covariant Wigner function for the spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field and its relation to the spin density matrix and the mean spin polarization vector. We obtain a formula relating the covariant Wigner function to the mean spin vector for a weakly interacting field. We then calculate the mean spin vector induced by thermal vorticity, thermal shear, and spin potential at local thermal equilibrium in the Belinfante, canonical and GLW pseudo-gauges. The resulting formula can be used to predict the spin polarization of spin-$3/2$ hadrons, such as the $\Omega^-$, in heavy-ion collisions. Differences in the thermal-shear induced polarization in the canonical and Belinfante pseudo-gauges make it possible to use local spin polarization measurements of the $\Omega^-$ to discriminate between the two pseudo-gauges.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Buzzegoli, Aleksandar Gecic, Rajeev Singh

item.title: Effects of Short-Range Correlations on Quarkyonic Matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.37502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we focus on investigating the impact of the short-range correlations on the properties of quarkyonic matter. These correlations induce the scattering of nucleons to momenta exceeding the Fermi momentum, thereby altering the momentum-space occupation distribution that underlies the quarkyonic framework. In particular, we examine to what extent the emergence of a high-momentum tail, due to the short-range nucleon-nucleon correlations, in the momentum distribution, for momenta exceeding the Fermi momentum, affects the fundamental properties of quarkyonic matter, such as the energy density, pressure, and speed of sound, among others. In fact, at high densities, the behavior of the momentum distribution has been established, both experimentally and theoretically, to follow a characteristic $\sim 1/k^4$ dependence at large momenta. To the best of our knowledge, this effect on quarkyonic matter has not yet been systematically investigated. Moreover, this experimentally confirmed feature of the momentum distribution suggests that heavy-ion collisions may probe quarkyonic matter, underscoring the importance of incorporating short-range correlations into a complete quarkyonic model.
item.dc:creator: K. Folias, Ch. C. Moustakidis

item.title: Axions from Betelgeuse: Probing Axion Couplings with $^{23}\rm{Na}$ and $^{55}\rm{Mn}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.34540v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate axion-like particle (ALP) production in the interior of Betelgeuse via nuclear de-excitation of thermally populated excited states of $^{23}$Na and $^{55}$Mn. As these ALPs propagate to Earth, they can produce photons either through their conversion in the Galactic magnetic field or through their decay. Using INTEGRAL-ISGRI and NuSTAR observations, we search for these photon signals, find no significant excess, and derive 95% CL exclusion limits on the ALP couplings. For magnetic-field conversion of ALPs, the $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ ($^{55}\mathrm{Mn}$) line observed with INTEGRAL-ISGRI constrains $|g_{a\gamma}g_{ap}| < 4.1\times10^{-21}$ ($6.9\times10^{-19}$) $\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ for $m_a < 10^{-10} \mathrm{eV}$. For ALP decays, the $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ ($^{55}\mathrm{Mn}$) line observed with INTEGRAL-ISGRI (NuSTAR) constrains $|g_{a\gamma}g_{ap}|$ down to $3.0\times10^{-22}$ ($2.9\times10^{-19}$) $\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ at $m_a \simeq 400$ ($83$) keV, weakening in both cases as $m_a^{-3/2}$ for lower ALP masses, and as $m_a^{-2}$ for $^{23}$Na below $m_a \sim 1$ keV, with sensitivity extending to $m_a \simeq 440.2$ ($124$) keV. Although our $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$-based limits are the strongest for both channels, their larger transition energy makes them more sensitive to the precise evolutionary stage of Betelgeuse, whereas the $^{55}\mathrm{Mn}$-based limits are considerably more robust against such uncertainties.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas A. M. Revel, Baldeep Grewal, Anupam Ray, Aaron C. Vincent

item.title: Beta decay of potassium-54 reveals the role of two-body currents in neutron-rich nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.36218v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The beta decay of neutron-rich nuclei probes the microscopic nature of weak interactions in the nuclear medium under extreme conditions. Such weak decays drive the synthesis of heavy elements in astrophysical environments, but remain poorly understood. Far from stability, experimental data are scarce, placing strong demands on ab initio nuclear theory. Two-body weak currents have been proposed as the dominant mechanism responsible for the universal quenching of theoretically predicted Gamow-Teller decay strength. However, direct experimental validation in neutron-rich nuclei has been lacking. Here we measure the beta decay of 54K, a nucleus at the experimental frontier of radioactive ion-beam facilities. In this work, the doubly magic nature of the daughter nucleus 54Ca results in a remarkably simple decay pattern, dominated by a single transition to a neutron-unbound state at 6.2 MeV with a comparative partial half-life logft=4.4(1) or Gamow-Teller decay strength B(GT)=0.26 (+0.08) (-0.04). Our measurement is reproduced by new state-of-the-art calculations of the decay, providing direct evidence for the essential role of two-body currents in nuclear beta decay for systems with a significant neutron excess. We establish a key benchmark for theoretical predictions of weak processes in exotic nuclei.

item.title: Subpercent accuracy in molecular electric quadrupole coupling: nuclear-size and relativistic effects in RaF
item.description: arXiv:2610.36286v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report a benchmark study of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine interaction in the electronic ground state of the RaF molecule, including finite-nuclear-size effects. The calculations include relativistic effects using the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian and electron correlation up to perturbative quadruple excitations within the coupled cluster framework. At the achieved level of accuracy, penetration of the electronic density into the finite nuclear quadrupole distribution produces a non-negligible correction to the usual electric field gradient (EFG) description at the center of the nucleus and must be considered. At a fixed rms charge radius, the EFG is much less sensitive to the shape of the monopole nuclear charge distribution: electron wavefunctions computed using the Gaussian and Fermi nuclear charge models yield nearly identical EFGs. The recommended effective EFG parameter for the $X\,{}^{2}\Sigma_{1/2}$ electronic ground state is $\langle q\rangle_0=-5.178(21)$ a.u., with an estimated uncertainty reduced by an order of magnitude compared to previous studies. Combined with future measurements of electric-quadrupole hyperfine coupling constants in RaF, this result can be used to determine the nuclear quadrupole moments of Ra isotopes with record precision.
item.dc:creator: Leonid V. Skripnikov, Michail Athanasakis-Kaklamanakis, Carlos M. Fajardo-Zambrano

item.title: Quark Saturation in Magnetized Pure Neutron Matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.36316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how magnetic fields affect the onset of quark saturation, which limits the domain of applicability of a purely baryonic description. We consider matter composed of electrically neutral $ddu$ baryons, including neutron- and $\Delta^0$-like states. Using a simple constituent-quark model, we compute the baryon wave functions and spectra in magnetic fields. The magnetic field polarizes the spin-flavor structure, compresses the internal wave function in the transverse direction, and strongly suppresses the transverse kinetic energy. From the baryon wave functions, we construct the one-body reduced density matrix and derive the corresponding single-quark distributions in longitudinal momentum and Landau-level space. We then use these distributions to evaluate quark occupation probabilities in an ideal baryon gas and determine the onset of quark saturation. At finite magnetic field in the $+z$-direction, the $d_\downarrow$ quark in the lowest Landau level reaches saturation first. The resulting saturation density depends nonmonotonically on the magnetic-field strength: it decreases at weak fields and increases at stronger fields. This behavior reflects the competition between spin-flavor polarization, which promotes saturation, and transverse spatial squeezing, which delays saturation by broadening of the quark transverse momentum distribution.
item.dc:creator: Toru Kojo

item.title: Nuclear Data Evaluation Utilizing Bayesian Monte Carlo Methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.36338v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While the body of experimental nuclear data continues to grow at a rapid pace, significant gaps persist. The lack of evaluated experimental data is far more pronounced in charged-particle reactions which are essential to a large portion of the isotope production community for vital medical, industrial, and national security interests. In the absence of experimental and evaluated data, isotope production relies on theoretical models that may result in low yield and isotopic impurities. This work investigates model and parameter adjustments in TALYS 2.0 to establish uncertainty bands on proton-induced cross sections, highlight influential parameters in calculations, and constrain adjustments within physically defensible bounds. The EXFOR dataset for proton-induced reactions on natural copper, comprised of 24 independent cross sections, was used for iterative Bayesian model updating. Upon convergence, parameters and their uncertainties were compared against 23 cumulative cross sections from EXFOR, highlighting the limitations of generalization. Various machine learning models were leveraged to predict TALYS performance, with a small neural network showing useful ranking capabilities across several generations, suggesting the use of a surrogate approach to screening for future evaluations.
item.dc:creator: Catherine E. Apgar, Lee A. Bernstein, Yun-Hsuan Lee, Wilson Lin, Alan B. McIntosh, Dmitri G. Medvedev, Jonathan T. Morrell, Ellen M. O'Brien, C. Etienne Vermeulen, Andrew S. Voyles

item.title: Energy density in color string clusters and its implications for heavy-quark energy loss
item.description: arXiv:2610.36723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Initial stages of relativistic ion and proton-proton collisions can be described within the framework of color flux tube formation between the receding color charges. In the approximation of fully penetrable color string volumes, regions of high string density yield overlaps of randomly oriented color fields and create string clusters. The paper discusses two ways of characterizing the medium formed by the resulting field configurations. One is based on the chromo-electric field strength that scales as the square root of the number of color sources in the cluster. The other is defined by the energy density of the confined color field and thus scales linearly with that number. We compare the effect of the two approaches on the extracted effective temperature of the medium, which is the input for calculations of collisional and radiative energy loss of a probe traversing it.
item.dc:creator: Daria Prokhorova, Shuzhe Shi, Evgeny Andronov

item.title: Improved nonflow control for multiparticle correlators and system-size-dependent evolution from OO to Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2610.36922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multiparticle correlations of event-plane angles, known as symmetry plane correlators (SPCs), and correlations of anisotropic flow amplitudes of different harmonics, known as symmetric cumulants (SCs), help constrain the initial conditions and the transport properties of the system formed in heavy-ion collisions. Such multiparticle correlations are robust against nonflow biases in heavy-ion collisions; however, in small systems the nonflow contribution is sizeable and can distort SPCs and SCs at low multiplicity, mimicking a flow-like signal. Evidence of nuclear-geometry-induced collectivity in light-ion collisions, such as OO and Ne--Ne, has been established at the LHC. Measurements of SPCs and SCs in these systems, and their comparison to heavy-ion collisions, can therefore clarify the system-size dependence of these correlations and the strength of nonlinear mode coupling. In this work, an improved nonflow subtraction framework based on multiplicity reweighting ($\czero$) and $v_1$-estimator-based ($\cone$) scaling is validated for selected SPCs and SCs using a controlled toy model and the \textsc{Pythia~8~Angantyr} model, where collective flow is absent by construction. We find that $\cone$ provides the more reliable nonflow control and apply it to predict the SPCs and normalized SCs in OO collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$~TeV with the \textsc{ampt} string-melting model. The results are compared with published Pb--Pb measurements from ALICE and from \textsc{ampt} as a function of midrapidity charged-particle multiplicity $\langle N_{\rm ch}\rangle(|\eta|<0.5)$, placing light- and heavy-ion systems on a common system-size axis.
item.dc:creator: Neelkamal Mallick, Suraj Prasad

item.title: Quasiparticle Modeling of Strange Quark Stars with In-Medium QCD Effects at Finite Temperature and Strong Magnetic Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.36953v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work investigates the properties of spin polarized strange quark matter SQM and the resulting structure of strange quark stars SQSs within a thermodynamically self consistent quasiparticle framework. By developing a dynamic bag constant intrinsically coupled to the medium dependent reduction of quark effective masses we ensure strict internal thermodynamic consistency. This coupling gives rise to a distinct non monotonic behavior in the speed of sound significantly stiffening the Equation of State EoS at high densities. Consequently our model predicts maximum stable gravitational masses up to 2.19 Mo. These results demonstrate that hot magnetized SQM provides a robust and viable mechanism to explain ultra massive pulsars such as PSR J0740 6620 and PSR J0952 0607 without requiring unrealistic thermal or structural assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Yogesh Kumar, Mihir Arora, Manas Lohani, Poonam Jain, Pargin Bangotra, Rajeev

item.title: Higher-order strongly intensive observables for forward-backward multiplicity correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.37051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Forward-backward multiplicity correlations probe the longitudinal structure of particle production, but fluctuations in the number of emitting sources complicate their interpretation. Strongly intensive observables remove the contribution of source-number fluctuations at second order. Here we extend the construction to all cumulant orders. For independent identical sources whose emission law does not depend on the source count, we build a normalized hierarchy of strongly intensive observables with $n$ new algebraically independent quantities at order $n$. Every observable is normalized to unity for statistically independent particles, vanishes when both window multiplicities are fixed, and remains finite at equal positive window means. We give explicit expressions through fourth order and an all-order recursion. Analytical particle production models and PYTHIA calculations for $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=0.9$ and 13 TeV demonstrate the sensitivity to window geometry, event selection, and connected multiparticle correlations. Fits constrained by the mean multiplicities and second-order observables provide conditional higher-order benchmarks. Deviations of these benchmarks from the PYTHIA results test the assumed correlation hierarchy, subject to the quality of the lower-order fit. Preliminary ALICE measurements at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV are used to illustrate the corresponding model-dependent scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Andronov

item.title: Impact of Neutrino Trapping on the Equation of State and Structure of Hybrid Stars with 2SC Quark Matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.37360v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate how sensitive the effects of neutrino trapping on hot hybrid stars are to uncertainties in the hadronic and quark equations of state and in the thermodynamic construction of the hadron--quark transition. The hadronic phase is described by finite-temperature covariant density functional equations of state, and the quark phase by a three-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model with repulsive vector interactions and two-flavor color superconductivity. Because confinement is absent from the NJL model, an effective pressure shift $B^*$ is used phenomenologically to locate the deconfinement transition. We construct isentropic stellar equations of state with and without trapped electron neutrinos, vary the quark vector coupling and the nuclear symmetry-energy slope, and compare global with local conservation of electron-lepton number within phase coexistence. Neutrino trapping generically shifts deconfinement toward higher density throughout the parameter range considered. Increasing the vector interaction stiffens quark matter and raises the maximum stellar mass, but only moderately for the couplings studied. We also examine stronger diquark pairing and RG-consistent regularization, instead of sharp momentum cut-off: both affect the pairing gap, phase boundaries, and quark-core composition more strongly than they alter the qualitative trends of the stellar mass--radius sequences. Conversely, trapping reduces the sensitivity to the hadronic symmetry-energy slope because the enhanced proton fraction drives matter toward greater isospin symmetry. Global and local lepton-number prescriptions produce rather similar mass--radius relations but substantially different internal phase structures: global conservation leads to a considerably more extended mixed phase.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Sabatucci, Armen Sedrakian

item.title: Probing the inner disk edge of rotating neutron stars with dipole excitations in finite nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.37394v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The nuclear equation of state shapes both the structure of rapidly rotating neutron stars and the orbital motion in their surrounding spacetime. Its uncertainty affects the mass and radius at which the innermost stable circular orbit reaches the stellar surface, a condition that defines the transition between disks whose inner edge is set by the surface and those truncated by orbital instability. We quantify how measurements of the electric dipole polarizability of neutron-rich nuclei reduce the uncertainty in this transition and in the orbital properties at the disk inner edge. We compute uniformly rotating neutron stars in general relativity for a family of equations of state that systematically vary the symmetry energy, derived from relativistic energy density functionals with density-dependent point-coupling interactions. We compare the results for the full family with those for the subset consistent with the measured dipole polarizabilities of finite nuclei. The dipole polarizability constraint reduces the spread in transition mass and equatorial radius by factors of about seven to ten across the spin frequencies considered. Along this transition, it also confines the orbital frequency at the disk inner edge to a band narrower than $20$~Hz at each spin. Combined with a measured neutron-star spin, a kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillation interpreted as disk orbital motion further restricts the mass--radius region, allowing an independent mass estimate to probe the symmetry-energy constraint. The dipole response of finite nuclei thus informs both the structure of rotating neutron stars and the orbital properties of their inner accretion disks.
item.dc:creator: P. S. Koliogiannis, N. Paar

item.title: Deriving the anomalous Lorentz transformation and side jump using a trace method
item.description: arXiv:2004.08910v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The side jump in the anomalous Lorentz transformation, arising from the spin-orbit interactions, plays important roles in various intriguing physics, such as chiral vortical effects and spin polarization. In this work, the side jump of the spin-half particles is visualized and evaluated ab initio within Dirac theory, through a comprehensive study of the density $\psi^\dagger\psi$ and position $\int d^3x\psi^\dagger \mathbf{x}\psi$ of a wave packet under Lorentz transformation. A compact gamma-matrix representation of the Lorentz boost matrix of a Dirac spinor, $S(\boldsymbol{\eta})= h_{\boldsymbol\eta}^{\mu}\gamma_\mu \check{u}^\nu \gamma_\nu$, has been found. Based on this expression, a trace method has been developed to derive the anomalous Lorentz transformation of the center of the probability density of a spin-half fermion wave packet, and a compact analytical expression for the side jump has been obtained through a transparent and tractable derivation. The momentum width plays an important role in the side jump. For example, for Gaussian wave packets, increasing the width suppresses the displacement, while the side jump at fixed width depends nonmonotonically on mass, reaching a maximum at a finite mass. In the zero-width limit, the side jump takes a compact form perpendicular to both the Pauli-Lubanski vector and the boost direction, recovering the known result for a chiral particle.
item.dc:creator: Jin-Rui Wu, Feng Li, Shuai Y. F. Liu

item.title: Numerical study of the three-boson bound-state problem in partial-wave and vector-variable formulations
item.description: arXiv:2606.05028v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a systematic benchmark of the three-boson bound-state problem in momentum space, comparing one-dimensional (1D) spectator-amplitude, two-dimensional (2D) partial-wave, and three-dimensional (3D) vector-variable formulations. The benchmark controls the interaction representation by embedding the same finite partial-wave interaction space in each formulation, so that discrepancies reflect discretization, interpolation, and quadrature errors. This enables direct 1D--2D--3D comparisons for separable interactions, controlled 2D--3D tests for local interactions, and comparison with the full local interaction in the 3D vector-variable formulation. Binding energies agree at the $10^{-6}$~MeV level for the separable interactions. For the local interactions at $l_{\rm max}=12$, the 2D--3D differences are $2.2\times10^{-6}$~MeV for MT-V and $5.3\times10^{-5}$~MeV for MT-IV. The 2D and 3D equations are also solved in both $t$-matrix-driven and bare-potential-driven forms, whose agreement validates the permutation geometry, quadrature, and interpolation. Fourier transforms to coordinate space yield consistent norm decompositions and spatial observables, providing an independent check of the momentum-space solutions.
item.dc:creator: Wolfgang Schadow, Mohammadreza R. Hadizadeh

item.title: Transport simulations with a constrained momentum-dependent chiral mean-field equation of state at various isospin fractions
item.description: arXiv:2606.13415v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a comparison of the UrQMD model using a chiral mean field EoS (CMF) with flow and pion production data in heavy ion collisions at low beam energies $E_{\mathrm{lab}}=0.2-2.0 A$ GeV and varying iso-spin fraction. The CMF model parameters are constrained by known properties of the high density equation of state of QCD at varying iso-spin fractions. This allows us to calculate the equation of state as well as nuclear interactions for different physical systems like neutron stars and heavy ion collisions in a consistent way. It is found that heavy ion reactions at the upcoming FAIR facility will only have marginal sensitivity on the iso-spin dependence of the high-density equation of state. At lower beam energies, comparing to FOPI, HADES and S$\pi$rit data, the sensitivity is higher but the observed deviations and systematic uncertainties of the existing data are larger than the sensitivity to the symmetry energy.
item.dc:creator: Jan Steinheimer, Marcus Bleicher

item.title: Accelerator neutrinos as a probe of in-medium hyperon potentials
item.description: arXiv:2607.09255v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Charged-current (anti)neutrino interactions create Lambda and Sigma hyperons inside the nucleus, so the hyperons that reach a detector have crossed nuclear matter and carry the imprint of the in-medium potentials U_Y(rho) that also govern the appearance of hyperons in neutron stars. In the StrangeMC simulation of argon, the reconstructed Lambda yield and momentum and a kaon-vetoed Sigma+ tag respond to U_Lambda and U_Sigma at SBND and DUNE energies. A detector-level forecast, with the production cross sections, fluxes and efficiencies as nuisance parameters and the muon kinematics calibrating the production model, determines U_Lambda at rho* = 0.82 rho_0, independently of the low-density exponent of the potential, to 1.5 MeV statistically and +-31 MeV in total. The largest item, 18 MeV, is the convention by which the cascade applies the potential. The measurement is a check, with different systematics, of the hypernuclear constraint, +-3.3 MeV at rho*, for momentum-independent potentials; U_Sigma is not determined. In the relativistic mean-field equations of state GM1 and FSU2H, anchored to the hypernuclear and Sigma-atom depths, the maximum neutron-star mass depends on the Lambda NN repulsion, which these data do not constrain.
item.dc:creator: Jaroslaw A. Nowak

item.title: Neutrino-induced hyperon final-state interactions as a probe of the in-medium hyperon potential
item.description: arXiv:2607.09273v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hyperon single-particle potentials U_Y(rho) govern hyperon propagation in nuclei and the appearance of hyperons in dense matter, where they soften the neutron-star equation of state (EOS) and lower the maximum mass M_max, the hyperon puzzle. Charged-current (anti)neutrino interactions on argon-40 create Lambda and Sigma hyperons inside the nucleus. The reconstructed Lambda yield and momentum and a kaon-vetoed final-state-interaction (FSI) Sigma+ tag respond to U_Lambda and U_Sigma at SBND and DUNE energies. We write the potential at low density as U_Y = U_Y(rho_0) (rho/rho_0)^gamma, plus a correction that vanishes at saturation. A detector-level Fisher forecast, with production cross sections, fluxes and efficiencies as nuisance parameters and the muon kinematics calibrating the production model, determines U_Lambda best at rho* = 0.82 rho_0, independently of gamma. The statistical precision is 1.5 MeV; with the production model profiled and the remaining systematic uncertainties added in quadrature, the total is +-31 MeV, of which the largest item, 18 MeV, is the convention by which the cascade applies the potential. The measurement is a check, with different systematics, of the hypernuclear constraint, +-3.3 MeV at rho*. U_Sigma is not constrained. In relativistic mean-field EOSs anchored to hypernuclear and Sigma-atom depths, M_max for n p Lambda Sigma- matter is 1.94 M_sun for GM1 and 2.03 M_sun for FSU2H with the phi meson; it depends on a high-density Lambda NN term c_Lambda that the neutrino data do not constrain. The calculations use the StrangeMC Monte Carlo generator.
item.dc:creator: Jaroslaw A. Nowak

item.title: Ancilla-recycled RODEO filtering for nuclear scattering: A cross-platform benchmark on quantum processors
item.description: arXiv:2608.26569v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum computation of trapped spectra for nuclear scattering requires resource-efficient circuits and reliable energy inputs. We present a cross-platform benchmark of ancilla-recycled RODEO filtering for a four-dimensional effective Hamiltonian describing a trapped neutron--proton model. Static circuits on IonQ Forte-1 and dynamic circuits on IBM Aachen implement the same ideal ten-cycle all-zero accepted filter using twelve and three active qubits, respectively. Mid-circuit measurement and reset reduce the active qubit count by 75\% while retaining all controlled evolutions. The interleaved IBM peak-center offset from the exact level is $-0.017 \pm 0.507~\mathrm{keV}$, compared with $-0.568 \pm 0.694~\mathrm{keV}$ for IonQ (finite-shot bootstrap uncertainties). At \(\omega=3.7~\mathrm{MeV}\), the modified effective range expansion maps both centers to finite-confinement scattering inputs consistent with the exact reference within propagated uncertainties. Three IBM batches exhibit center variations beyond finite-shot uncertainties (\(p=0.015\)), despite comparatively stable postselection amplitudes. Calibration-derived noisy simulations do not consistently reproduce the measured centers. Complete sampled support enables sample-based quantum diagonalization to recover the exact effective-space level, whereas larger-space simulator tests expose substantial errors from omitted configurations. The calculation validates one finite-confinement input, not a free-space phase shift. This benchmark provides a reusable circuit and validation protocol separating spectral precision, hardware repeatability, and sampled-subspace completeness for multilevel nuclear-scattering calculations.
item.dc:creator: Myeong-Hwan Mun, Jubin Park, Myung-Ki Cheoun, Eunja Ha

item.title: Dynamical Coulomb effects on charged-pion HBT-radius splitting in central Au+Au collisions at few-GeV energies
item.description: arXiv:2609.23422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The pair transverse momentum ($k_T$) and collision-energy ($\sqrt{s_{NN}}$) dependent difference between $\pi^{+}\pi^{+}$ and $\pi^{-}\pi^{-}$ femtoscopic correlations was observed by the HADES and STAR Collaborations. We investigate how much of the observed splitting can be accounted for by Coulomb dynamics in 0-10\% central Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.42$-5.2 GeV. Using the UrQMD model and the CRAB programme, three transport scenarios that successively include baryon-baryon, baryon-meson, and meson-meson Coulomb interactions are considered. In a separate calculation based on the baryon-baryon reference, we reconstruct the time-dependent effective charge $Z_{\rm{eff}}(t)$ and radius $R_{\rm{eff}}(t)$ of the residual charged source and propagate each pion from its individual last strong-interaction point through the evolving field. The calculations reproduce the main $k_{T}$ and $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ dependences of the radii. Baryon--meson Coulomb interactions generate most of the additional charge splitting in the microscopic calculation. The residual-source treatment also enhances the longitudinal and sideward radius ratios relative to the reference, whereas the outward ratio changes little, and the enhancement generally decreases with increasing $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$. Within the present framework, this contribution does not fully account for the data, motivating further investigation of the charged-source geometry and its interplay with strong-interaction dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Pengcheng Li, Yongjia Wang, Qingfeng Li

item.title: Photoproduction of $J/\Psi$ in peripheral Oxygen-Oxygen collisions
item.description: arXiv:2605.12123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The photoproduction of $J/\Psi$ in peripheral Oxygen - Oxygen ($OO$) collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is investigated considering distinct assumptions for the modeling of the nuclear photon flux, overlap function and dipole - proton scattering amplitude. Predictions for the associated rapidity distributions and total cross - sections are presented. Our results indicate that the experimental study of the photoproduction of $J/\Psi$ in peripheral $OO$ collisions is, in principle, feasible. In addition, they point out that the combination of the results for this final state in $OO$ collisions with those obtained for $PbPb$ collisions will allow us to derive important constraints on the description of photon - induced process at peripheral collisions.
item.dc:creator: Pedro E. A. da Costa, Andr\'e V. Giannini, Victor P. Gon\c{c}alves, Bruno D. Moreira

item.title: Radiative Corrections to Elastic Lepton-Proton Scattering with Focus on Two-Photon-Exchange Diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2605.31123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Lepton (electron and muon) scattering experiments are excellent tools to gain insight into the nucleon structure. Elastic electron-proton scattering probes the spatial distribution of charge and magnetization inside the proton, and comparing electron-proton and muon-proton scattering data tests lepton universality. The availability of a plethora of scattering data with increased precision and observed discrepancies such as the proton form factor puzzle and the proton radius puzzle motivated a renewed effort to improve the theoretical framework. Realizing that the one-photon-exchange approximation (OPE), i.~e. the Born approximation, is not sufficient, radiative corrections in QED, especially the two-photon-exchange (TPE) diagrams, are under investigation. The TPE diagrams are of special interest among the radiative corrections, since their hadronic-structure-dependent contribution generates an additional dependence of the cross section on the virtual-photon polarization parameter beyond the Born approximation that is not captured by standard model-independent radiative correction procedures, and that directly impacts the extraction of proton form factors. In this work, we present a complete calculation of QED radiative corrections to elastic electron-proton and muon-proton scattering at next-to-leading order, taking into account loop-momentum-dependent form factors. In the discussion of their numerical impact on lepton-proton scattering cross sections, we pay special attention to the elastic nucleon contribution to the TPE diagrams and compare them with existing theoretical predictions and lepton-proton scattering data.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Crowe, Syed Mehedi Hasan, Doreen Wackeroth

item.title: The QCD phase diagram for three-flavor M\"obius domain-wall fermions
item.description: arXiv:2606.28086v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the phase transition of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) with three degenerate quark flavors at zero baryon chemical potential. Using M\"{o}bius domain-wall fermions as the lattice fermion formulation, we ensure excellent chiral symmetry preservation. Our simulations are performed at three different temporal lattice extents, $N_{t}=6, 8, 12$, with a fixed lattice spacing $a=0.1361(20)$ fm, corresponding to temperatures of 242(4), 181(3), and 121(2) MeV, respectively. We explore a range of quark masses and spatial volumes with aspect ratios $N_{s}/N_{t}$ spanning from 2 to 4. By analyzing the mass and volume dependencies of the plaquette, plaquette susceptibility, chiral condensate, chiral susceptibilities, and Binder cumulant, we identify the pseudocritical transition quark masses from our largest lattice volumes. For $N_t=6$, this is 184(10) MeV (determined from the plaquette susceptibility). For $N_t=8$ and 12, the transition points vary slightly depending on whether the total or disconnected chiral susceptibility is used, yielding ranges of 36(1)-39.1(9) MeV and 3.5(3)-3.7(2) MeV, respectively, in the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme at a scale of $\mu=2$ GeV. The negligible volume dependence at $N_t=6$ and 8, combined with finite-size scaling analysis at $N_t=12$ revealing volume growth significantly weaker than expected for a first- or second-order phase transition, points to a continuous crossover at these specific quark mass points. Additionally, we study the effects of residual chiral symmetry breaking on the chiral condensate and chiral susceptibilities using two different values of $L_s$.
item.dc:creator: Yu Zhang, Yasumichi Aoki, Jishnu Goswami, Shoji Hashimoto, Issaku Kanamori, Takashi Kaneko, Yoshifumi Nakamura
